games.title: Minecraft
games.note: Markus Persson posted the first version on the TIGSource forums in May 2009; it became the best-selling video game ever.

games.title: Minecraft Dungeons
games.note: A Diablo-style dungeon crawler set in Minecraft's world, for up to four players.

games.title: Infiniminer
games.note: A team-based block-mining game; its source code leaked and development stopped soon after release.

games.title: Team Fortress 2
games.note: A cartoon-styled team shooter with nine classes; it became free to play in 2011.

games.title: Motherload
games.note: A Flash game where you drill ever deeper into Mars for minerals while managing fuel and hull damage.

games.title: Dwarf Fortress
games.note: Free for 16 years, it simulates whole worlds with histories; a graphical Steam version arrived in 2022.

games.title: RollerCoaster Tycoon
games.note: Chris Sawyer wrote almost all of it by himself in assembly language.

games.title: Transport Tycoon
games.note: A business sim of rail, road, sea and air networks; fans later remade it as the free OpenTTD.

games.title: Dungeon Keeper
games.note: You play the villain: dig a dungeon, attract monsters and fend off heroes, even possessing creatures in first person.

games.title: Populous
games.note: Peter Molyneux's game where you play a god reshaping the land so your followers can multiply.

games.title: Terraria
games.note: Andrew Spinks's 2D digging and boss-fighting game; it has sold more than 50 million copies.

games.title: Starbound
games.note: A 2D sandbox spread across procedurally generated planets, reached by your own starship.

games.title: Core Keeper
games.note: A top-down underground mining sandbox from Linköping, Sweden, for up to eight players.

games.title: Luanti
games.note: A free, open-source voxel game engine, called Minetest until 2024.

games.title: Roblox
games.note: Created by David Baszucki and Erik Cassel; nearly all of its games are made by players.

games.title: Garry's Mod
games.note: Began as a free Half-Life 2 mod in December 2004; a paid standalone version followed in 2006.

games.title: s&box
games.note: Garry Newman's successor to Garry's Mod, announced in 2017 and released in April 2026.

games.title: Lego Worlds
games.note: A brick-building sandbox that came to consoles when it left early access in 2017.

games.title: Dragon Quest Builders
games.note: Rebuilds the ruined world of the first Dragon Quest one block at a time.

games.title: Dragon Quest Builders 2
games.note: Added online co-op building and a story tied to Dragon Quest II.

games.title: Fortnite: Save the World
games.note: Announced in 2011; the free Battle Royale mode spun off from it two months after its paid launch.

games.title: Lego Fortnite
games.note: A survival-crafting game made with the Lego Group and played inside Fortnite.

games.title: Valheim
games.note: Made by a team of five in Skövde, Sweden; it sold five million copies in about a month.

games.title: Enshrouded
games.note: A co-op voxel survival RPG for up to 16 players, from the makers of Portal Knights.

games.title: Palworld
games.note: Creature-catching survival with guns; it sold 8 million copies on Steam in its first six days.

games.title: Craftopia
games.note: Pocketpair's earlier open-world crafting game, mixing farming, automation and monster capture.

games.title: Vintage Story
games.note: A slow, demanding block-building survival game started by Tyron Madlener after his Minecraft mod Vintagecraft.

games.title: Hytale
games.note: Riot cancelled it in 2025; its founders bought it back and it reached early access in January 2026.

games.title: Robinson's Requiem
games.note: A first-person survival sim tracking hunger, thirst, fatigue and temperature; you can even perform surgery.

games.title: Deus
games.note: The PC-only sequel to Robinson's Requiem.

games.title: Survival Kids
games.note: A shipwrecked child crafts tools and finds food on a desert island.

games.title: Lost in Blue
games.note: Two teenagers stranded on an island forage, cook and build using the DS touch screen.

games.title: Don't Starve
games.note: Grew out of a 24-hour game jam Klei held while making Shank 2.

games.title: Don't Starve Together
games.note: The multiplayer version, in early access from December 2014 and fully released in 2016.

games.title: DayZ (standalone)
games.note: The standalone version of Dean Hall's mod entered early access in 2013 and reached 1.0 in 2018.

games.title: 7 Days to Die
games.note: Every seventh night a blood-moon horde attacks your base; it stayed in early access until 2024.

games.title: The Forest
games.note: After a plane crash your son is taken, and you must survive a forest full of cannibals.

games.title: Sons of the Forest
games.note: Sold two million copies in its first 24 hours in early access.

games.title: Trespasser
games.note: A Jurassic Park game with full physics and no HUD; health was shown as a tattoo on the heroine's chest.

games.title: ARK: Survival Evolved
games.note: Players tame dinosaurs to ride, fight and farm; it stayed in early access for over two years.

games.title: Subnautica
games.note: An ocean-planet survival game with no guns; early access began in 2014 and the full release came in 2018.

games.title: Subnautica: Below Zero
games.note: A standalone follow-up set in an icy region of the same planet, 4546B.

games.title: The Long Dark
games.note: Raphael van Lierop's survival game set in the Canadian wilderness after a mysterious geomagnetic disaster.

games.title: Raft
games.note: Began as a university project; you survive at sea by hooking floating debris to grow your raft.

games.title: Grounded
games.note: Four kids shrunk to the size of ants survive in a suburban backyard; inspired by Honey, I Shrunk the Kids.

games.title: Green Hell
games.note: Amazon rainforest survival where you inspect your body for leeches and wounds and keep an eye on your sanity.

games.title: Conan Exiles
games.note: Creative director Joel Bylos said the European migrant crisis partly inspired its setting of exiles.

games.title: Icarus
games.note: Dean Hall's session-based survival game: players drop to a hostile planet for timed missions.

games.title: Unturned
games.note: A free blocky zombie-survival game, released when its Calgary creator was sixteen.

links.took: Two teams with distinct roles competing; Barth named Team Fortress 2 as an inspiration.
links.added: Teams race to dig out ore in a fully diggable world made of blocks.

links.took: Digging down through layers of ground to collect valuable minerals.
links.added: A first-person view, team multiplayer and a 3D world built from blocks.

links.took: First-person mining and building in a world made of blocks.
links.added: Single-player crafting, monsters at night and endless generated terrain.

src.t: PC Gamer: The first moments of Minecraft

links.extra: Infiniminer came out in April 2009; Persson posted the first Minecraft version that May.

links.took: Digging, building and simulated survival; Persson first aimed for a 'lightweight Dwarf Fortress'.
links.added: Kept it simple and accessible, with the player digging and building in first person.

src.t: Markus Persson, interview by Alex Handy, Game Developer (Gamasutra), 2010

links.extra: Persson called Dwarf Fortress and roguelikes some of the biggest inspirations for Minecraft's gameplay.

links.took: The isometric 3D look of Persson's first prototype, RubyDung.
links.added: A first-person world built and reshaped one block at a time.

src.t: Markus Persson, interview by Alex Handy, Game Developer (Gamasutra), 2010

links.extra: Persson described the early idea as if Dwarf Fortress and RollerCoaster Tycoon 'had a baby'.

links.took: Digging out tunnels and rooms; Persson also tried a first-person view like Dungeon Keeper's.
links.added: The player digs and builds personally instead of commanding imps and monsters.

src.t: Markus Persson, interview by Alex Handy, Game Developer (Gamasutra), 2010

links.extra: Persson said the similarity to Dungeon Keeper was what most drew him to Dwarf Fortress.

links.took: Chris Sawyer's isometric business-sim style; he conceived RCT after Transport Tycoon's success.
links.added: Theme parks with roller coasters you design piece by piece, and guests with moods.
links.extra: Sawyer used Transport Tycoon money to tour theme parks and grew fond of roller coasters he once hated.

links.took: Bullfrog's god's-eye view of shaping land and directing creatures from above.
links.added: Playing the villain: digging a dungeon to lure monsters and kill heroes.

links.took: Large fantasy worlds to explore, which Tarn Adams cited as inspiring his world generation.
links.added: Whole worlds generated with centuries of history before play begins.
links.extra: Adams cited the Ultima series in general.

links.took: A detailed body-part and wound system from the tabletop RPG.
links.added: Simulated injuries down to individual organs and bones for every creature.

links.took: Deep simulated systems and digging, later credited by Terraria's developers as an influence.
links.added: Fast 2D action with mining, crafting and boss fights.

src.t: Wikipedia: Dwarf Fortress (influence on later games)

links.extra: Terraria's developers praised Dwarf Fortress at its 2022 Steam release and cited its influence.

links.took: Digging, crafting and building in a world made of blocks.
links.added: A side-on 2D view, many weapons and bosses, and goals Spinks felt Minecraft lacked.

src.t: Wikipedia: Minecraft (lists Terraria among its clones)

links.extra: Spinks said a big reason he started Terraria was that he missed a bigger purpose in Minecraft.

links.took: 2D digging, crafting and combat; director Finn 'Tiyuri' Brice had drawn art for Terraria.
links.added: A starship and procedurally generated planets across a whole galaxy.

src.t: Wikipedia: Starbound (IGN compared it to Terraria)

links.took: Underground mining, crafting and boss progression; critics called it a 'top-down Terraria'.
links.added: A top-down view, farming and cooking, and up to eight players in one cave world.

links.took: Block-based digging and crafting mechanics.
links.added: A cozy top-down underground world with bosses and automation.

links.took: Minecraft's world, creatures and blocky look.
links.added: A dungeon crawler with loot and four-player co-op.

links.took: Block-based building and survival, closely modeled on Minecraft.
links.added: Free, open-source code and a platform for many player-made games.

src.t: Wikipedia: Minecraft (lists Luanti, formerly Minetest, among its clones)

links.took: Nelson Sexton's start: his zombie-survival Roblox game Deadzone, which resembled Unturned.
links.added: A standalone free game with blocky graphics, crafting and online servers.

links.took: Zombie survival with looting and other players, popularized by DayZ.
links.added: Simple blocky graphics that run on modest PCs, free to play.

src.t: Wikipedia: Unturned (reviewers compared it to DayZ and Minecraft)

links.took: Valve's Source engine and physics, plus Half-Life 2's props and characters.
links.added: No goals at all: a physics sandbox for contraptions and player-made game modes.
links.extra: Half-Life 2 came out in November 2004; the first Garry's Mod followed on 24 December.

links.took: Facepunch's team and the success Garry's Mod brought the studio.
links.added: An online survival game of gathering, building and raiding other players.

links.took: Garry Newman's sandbox tools and player-made game modes.
links.added: A new engine built on Source 2 and a platform for sharing whole games.
links.extra: Announced in 2017 as a successor, it was released in April 2026.

links.took: Radiation zones and harsh open-world survival; Newman likened Rust to S.T.A.L.K.E.R.
links.added: Player-built bases and raids, with the world shaped by its players.

src.t: Engadget, 2013: Garry's Mod creator launches Rust in free alpha

links.extra: Wikipedia says Newman described Rust as closer to S.T.A.L.K.E.R. after moving away from DayZ.

links.took: Harvesting resources and crafting tools and buildings.
links.added: A brutal online world where other players are the main threat.

src.t: Game Informer, 2013: Rust is Minecraft meets Stalker meets DayZ

links.took: An open building sandbox, made after a planned Lego and Minecraft collaboration fell through.
links.added: Lego bricks, minifigures and vehicles in procedurally made worlds.
links.extra: IGN and Polygon framed it as Lego's answer to Minecraft.

links.took: Block-by-block building and gathering, which led press to call it a Dragon Quest Minecraft.
links.added: A story-driven RPG campaign with quests, towns to rebuild and boss fights.

links.took: The world of the first Dragon Quest, Alefgard, and its monsters.
links.added: Retold as a building game, set after the hero failed to save the world.

links.took: Block building combined with an RPG story.
links.added: Online co-op building and a much bigger island to shape.

links.took: Gathering and building; Tim Sweeney called the game 'Minecraft meets Left 4 Dead'.
links.added: Building forts against waves of zombie-like husks, with shooting and hero classes.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fortnite: Save the World (Tim Sweeney, Roger Collum)

links.took: Four-player co-op against hordes, the other half of Sweeney's pitch.
links.added: Fort building and traps prepared before each wave arrives.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fortnite: Save the World (Tim Sweeney)

links.took: Third-person shooting, which producer Roger Collum said it mixed with building games.
links.added: A cartoon look and building walls and ramps in the middle of fights.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fortnite: Save the World (Roger Collum)

links.took: The building-game half of the mix, named by producer Roger Collum with Minecraft.
links.added: Combined with third-person shooting, like 'peanut butter cups', Collum said.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fortnite: Save the World (Roger Collum)

links.took: Save the World's building system, weapons and art, reused by Epic.
links.added: A free 100-player last-one-standing mode that soon outgrew its parent game.
links.extra: Save the World entered paid early access in July 2017; Battle Royale followed in September.

links.took: Fortnite's platform, characters and building, inside the same game.
links.added: A Lego-styled survival-crafting world with villages to grow.

links.took: Exploration-led adventure in a world that rewards curiosity more than survival chores.
links.added: Viking co-op survival, base building and boss-gated biomes in a procedural world.
links.extra: Iron Gate said Zelda and Skyrim were bigger influences than other survival games.

links.took: Nordic fantasy and the pull of exploring a single-player RPG world.
links.added: Up to ten players building longhouses and sailing between islands.

links.took: Survival crafting and base building, a genre Minecraft popularized.
links.added: Norse myth, boss-gated progression and sailing in a procedurally generated world.

src.t: Wikipedia: Survival game (Minecraft widely credited with popularizing the genre)

links.extra: Iron Gate says Zelda and Skyrim mattered more to Valheim than survival games did.

links.took: Climbing and gliding exploration across a large handmade fantasy map.
links.added: Voxel building you can reshape freely, and a poisonous fog called the Shroud.

links.took: Co-op survival crafting with base building and boss progression.
links.added: Fully reshapeable voxel terrain, RPG skill trees and handcrafted quests.

links.took: Stamina-based melee combat with dodging and blocking, toned down in difficulty.
links.added: Survival crafting and building wrapped around that combat.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the combat drew on 'Soulsborne' games without matching their difficulty.

links.took: Open-world survival crafting with taming and base building; Mizobe said Palworld plays more like ARK.
links.added: Cute creatures called Pals that fight, farm and work in factories, plus guns.

links.took: Pocketpair's experience making an open-world survival crafting game.
links.added: Creature collecting at the core, with Pals doing the base work.

src.t: Game Informer, 2023: Creature Feature, the story of Palworld

links.took: Catching and collecting creatures to fight alongside you.
links.added: Survival crafting, guns and creatures put to work in bases.

src.t: Takuro Mizobe, via My Nintendo News, Jan 2024

links.extra: Mizobe called Pokémon a 'great predecessor' but said Palworld's mechanics are closer to ARK.

links.took: It began as a standalone version of Tyron Madlener's Minecraft mod Vintagecraft.
links.added: Its own engine and slower survival with seasons, smithing and pottery.

links.took: Block-based building and adventure; its team ran Hypixel, a popular Minecraft server.
links.added: Built-in creation tools for minigames and adventure zones with bosses.

src.t: Insider Gaming, 2025: Hytale early access release date

links.extra: Press describes it as a Minecraft-inspired survival crafting sandbox.

links.took: Konami's desert-island survival with foraging and crafting.
links.added: Two stranded teens working together, using the DS touch screen.

links.took: Desperate island survival: foraging, cooking and staying alive day to day.
links.added: A gothic, Tim Burton-like art style and harsh permanent death.

src.t: Kevin Forbes (Klei), Road to the IGF, Gamasutra, 2012

links.took: The tense first night, when you scramble to survive in an unknown world.
links.added: Hunger, sanity and seasons in a hand-drawn wilderness.

src.t: Kevin Forbes (Klei), Road to the IGF, Gamasutra, 2012
MCV: Minecraft + Tim Burton = Don't Starve

links.extra: Forbes said he loved Minecraft's first night, when creepers attack and you learn to build a shelter.

links.took: Wilderness survival with hunger and sanity.
links.added: Online co-op for several players sharing one world.

links.took: First-person survival with bodily needs and injuries.
links.added: Continued Silmarils' survival simulation on PC.

links.took: Dean Hall's mod design: scarce loot, permadeath and tense meetings with strangers.
links.added: Its own engine work and map updates, sold separately from Arma 2.

links.took: Dean Hall's harsh survival design, now at his own studio RocketWerkz.
links.added: Timed missions on a hostile alien planet, returning to orbit between drops.

src.t: Wikipedia: Icarus (video game); RocketWerkz, Dean Hall

links.took: Voxel terrain you can dig into, build on and destroy.
links.added: Zombie hordes that attack your fort every seventh night.

src.t: The Fun Pimps' 2013 pitch, via Niche Gamer

links.extra: The developers also named the Fallout series as an influence.

links.took: Hordes of zombies that rush and swarm players.
links.added: Defending a player-built base, with crafting and RPG skills.

src.t: DSOGaming, 2013: 7 Days to Die pre-alpha footage

links.took: Free-form sandbox survival where you chop trees and build shelters.
links.added: First-person survival horror against cannibal tribes who watch and stalk you.
links.extra: Falcone also named the films The Descent and Cannibal Holocaust.

links.took: A first-person, physics-driven survival trek through hostile island wilds.
links.added: Base building, crafting and co-op play against cannibals instead of dinosaurs.

links.took: Cannibal survival horror, crafting and log-built bases.
links.added: Companions like Kelvin who follow orders, and a larger island.

links.took: First-person survival crafting against hostile tribes, popularized by The Forest.
links.added: Amazon rainforest realism: parasites, wound care, nutrition and a sanity meter.

links.took: Online survival with gathering, base building and player raids.
links.added: Taming dinosaurs to ride, fight and farm resources.

links.took: Wilderness survival crafting, which Rapczak listed among ARK's influences.
links.added: 3D dinosaurs and an online world of player tribes.

links.took: A little of Pokémon's creature collecting, by Rapczak's own account.
links.added: Taming wild dinosaurs by knocking them out and feeding them.

links.took: Open-ended gathering and crafting, the team's starting inspiration.
links.added: A handmade alien ocean, submarines and a story uncovered by diving deeper.
links.extra: Cleveland: 'We started by being inspired by Minecraft and Don't Starve.'

links.took: Survival with hunger, thirst and crafting in a strange world.
links.added: Fear of the deep, no guns and a hand-built ocean to explore.

links.took: Ocean survival, base building and vehicles on planet 4546B.
links.added: Icy land regions, a voiced lead character and a more direct story.

links.took: Ocean survival crafting, popularized by Subnautica, which critics often compare it to.
links.added: Survival on a small raft you grow by hooking floating debris, often in co-op.

links.took: First-person wilderness survival with hunger, cold and permanent death, popularized by DayZ.
links.added: Single-player, with no zombies: just cold, wolves and a quiet Canadian wilderness.

src.t: Wikipedia: Survival game (Minecraft and DayZ's success spurred many survival games from 2012)

links.took: Survival crafting and co-op base building, a genre Minecraft popularized.
links.added: Shrunk to insect size in a backyard, fighting spiders and building with grass blades.
links.extra: Brennecke called Minecraft probably one of the first big successes of the survival genre.

links.took: The feel of a fantasy RPG world, which Funcom wanted to blend with survival.
links.added: Brutal survival in Robert E. Howard's Hyborian world, with thralls and building.
links.extra: Bylos placed the game somewhere between Skyrim and ARK: Survival Evolved.

links.took: Online survival crafting with base building, raids and pets.
links.added: Enslaved 'thralls' who staff your base, and giant summoned gods in sieges.
